reasons: The cited clause (Section 20.1) contains only a one-way Customer indemnity for 'every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services' with no Vendor indemnity anywhere — squarely the rule's walk-away scenario, so a critical deviation finding is correctly classified, not over-flagging.

The redline reaches the preferred position: Vendor defence/indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics; and Customer's indemnity narrowed to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Inclusion of the usual exclusions (modification, combination, Customer specifications) and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies is fallback-consistent and also repairs the dangling Section 9.3 cross-reference to infringement remedies; the inserted remedies paragraph lands in the fifth position, matching the referenced 'Section 20.5'.

The failed minimal-edit check (0.606 changed-character ratio) is expected here: the rule requires rewriting the one-sided indemnity and inserting the missing Vendor obligation, and the surviving Customer indemnity retains its original operative structure.
Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, correctly prefixed, and states what changed and why with the playbook basis.

Minor drafting nit only (not a basis for failure): the inserted paragraphs are rendered without 20.2–20.5 numbering while the exclusions text cross-references 'Section 20.2(a)'; numbering should be confirmed on execution.
